set.descent_text: The route finishes with a class 4 scramble to the summit of Liberty Bell, so the way off is the normal summit descent rather than the face. From the top, head east and make a short series of single-rope rappels from fixed anchors (a 60 m rope is enough) into the Liberty-Concord notch. From the notch, descend the Beckey Gully to the Blue Lakes trail on the west side of the mountain, which is the opposite side from the East Face approach, so plan where packs and shoes will wait. Do not rappel the face itself, since apart from the shared stance with Liberty Crack its belays are not bolted.

review.notes: Freedom Rider page: 14th pitch is class 4 to the summit, regular east-face descent, few bolted belays. Descent details from Beckey Route and Overexposure pages; area page puts the Blue Lakes trailhead on the west side. Rappel count of three is from sibling Dark Side of Liberty; Beckey page describes two single-rope rappels, so counts vary.

set.descent_text: The route ends in easy fourth-class ground just below the summit, so use the normal Liberty Bell descent. From the top, retrace the ridge past the short slabby step, then follow the tree-filled gully east to the first bolted rappel station. A short series of single-rope rappels from fixed anchors, easily done with a 60 m rope, puts you in the Liberty-Concord notch at the top of the Beckey Gully. Scramble down the gully, taking care not to knock rocks onto parties below, and follow the trail back to the Blue Lakes trailhead.

review.notes: Sidewinder page: last pitch mostly 4th class toward the summit, starts from Beckey Gully. Rappel count and rope length from Beckey Route page; notch landing from Overexposure page.

set.descent_text: Rappel from the installed bolts on the ridge or downclimb the same broken rock and slabs to the saddle between Lundin Peak and East Lundin Peak. From the saddle, follow the climbers' path over to Red Pass, then take the Commonwealth Creek trail down to the PCT and out to the parking lot at the Snoqualmie Pass exit. Allow about two hours from East Lundin to the car. The three large bolts are best treated as landmarks and a rappel anchor to back up.

review.notes: MP East Ridge: saddle between Lundin and East Lundin, three bolts, approach via Red Pass; MP West Ridge: East Ridge descent and PCT lot logistics; Yellowleaf: rappel to saddle and 2h12 down from the East summit to the PCT trailhead.

set.descent_text: The route is bolted for rappelling and is designed to be descended on its own line with one 70 m rope. From the top anchors, rappel back down to the belay bolt on the small ledge at the base of the apron. The route runs almost directly below Ellen Pea, so that line can serve as an alternative way up or down. From the base, scramble down the Supercave gully, the reverse of the approach, to the pullout near milepost 166 on SR-20.

review.notes: MP route page: 3 pitches, rappelled with one 70 m rope, belay bolt at start, directly under Ellen Pea; area page: approach gully from milepost 166. The final scramble down is the reverse of that approach.

set.descent_text: Descend the standard East Ridge rather than the face. Downclimb the knife-edge summit ridge, which can be icy and firm late in the season, and drop through the gap in the lower ridge to the Inspiration Glacier. Rope up for the glacier, then follow the standard track down the Eldorado Glacier to Roush Basin, over the intervening ridge into Eldorado Creek Basin, and down the boulder field and timbered climbers' trail to the Cascade River crossing and trailhead. No rappels are needed. Snow bridges and crevasses weaken through the afternoon, so aim to be off the glaciers early.

review.notes: Descent is the East Ridge/Eldorado Glacier route used by the sibling routes; the NPS conditions page describes East Ridge and Eldorado Glacier travel and the NE Face beside it. A search summary of a Mountaineers trip report also says a NE Face party descended the East Ridge. Whether the face tops out on the summit itself is not stated in a page I read.

set.descent_text: Descend the way you came. From the summit, work back along the ramps and ledges on the southeast side to the false summit, then downclimb the class 3 rock of the southwest ridge to the col. The step between the two summits is very exposed and a fall there would be fatal, so move carefully and avoid wet rock. From the col, retrace the traverse to the upper col and descend the gully to the Access Creek meadows, which becomes a loose rock pile late in the season, so stay close together or out of each other's fall line and wear helmets. Then bushwhack back to Big Beaver Creek, ford it, and walk the Big Beaver trail out to the Ross Lake landing.

review.notes: WTA trip report (Sep 2014): ascent via col above Access Creek, class 3 SW ridge to false summit, exposed ramps on the SE face to the summit, descent along the same line, loose gully, return via Big Beaver. Single source.
